findings.title: Suffix heuristic labels actively consumed child contracts as historical evidence
findings.evidence: historical() classifies every tests/fixtures/*-contract.json as preserved-historical-evidence. inventory.json:2053 (seal-digest-law-contract.json) and :1260 (ed25519-acceptance-profile-contract.json) carry that label, yet the seal child CLI parses the seal contract for current profile/vector/decision identity (seal check-freeze.mjs:267-273) and the Ed25519 vectors pin the 0g2s contract as current fixture identity (vectors.json:13-14); the same applies to pacemaker, 0j-b, 0o-* and 0p* contracts consumed by current subsystem tests. Custody is byte-protected either way and README:135-136 keeps all preserved records byte-identical, so no preservation or authority error results; only the role label is imprecise.
findings.violated_requirement: Classification identifies current versus historical role (README:132-134)

findings.title: Accepted real root-config shape is not named as the grammar's positive baseline
findings.evidence: vite.config.mts:7-8 declares `const config = defineConfig({ plugins: [tsconfigPaths()], ... })`, :139 exports `workspaceAliases` derived from config.resolve.alias, and :141 exports default `config`. The existing root grammar requires a direct `export default defineConfig(` call (check-protocol-v3-freeze.mjs:367-383,469) and therefore already rejects the real file independently of the eight exclusions. README:78-86 lists what the closed grammar must reject (plugin/export/mutation changes) and requires accepting the real config, but does not name this exact const-plus-default-export, named re-export and tsconfigPaths plugin shape as the frozen positive control, which RED's lifecycle-incompatibility attribution and the grammar's positive test both depend on.
findings.violated_requirement: Closed selection grammar must accept the real config and reject the reviewed mutant set; attributable RED refusal

findings.title: Checkout for the single RED execution and the per-checkout typecheck stage mapping are implicit
findings.evidence: verification.md:14-15 runs the new suite once after static gates and :53-58 states all runtime suites use dedicated current-source checkouts with no direct-main runtime claim, but neither the RED entry (gate-plan.mjs:35) nor the text says the RED execution occurs in a prepared checkout rather than main. typecheck.mjs accepts stages baseline/green/isolated with one exclusive report per OUTPUT directory; which of main, A and B runs `green` versus `isolated` is left to stage custody. Neither point blocks authoring; both belong in the capsule freeze.
findings.violated_requirement: Explicit stage custody before execution; no direct-main runtime claim

findings.title: Semantic-only CODEOWNERS leaves newly byte-protected roots under the default owner rule
findings.evidence: The v3 CODEOWNERS block validated by the root (check-protocol-v3-freeze.mjs:165-180) covers 14 patterns; newlyByteProtectedPaths (inventory.json:3378-3416) and the supplements/scripts/workflow roots rely on the default `*` owner. Because CODEOWNERS is now semantic-source (:297-299) rather than byte-frozen, that default can change in-band, though any CODEOWNERS edit still needs the frozen cohort through the terminal `/CODEOWNERS` rule (:183) and byte-protected paths remain blocked by the root status regardless of approver. State this explicitly or extend the v3 block; not a security gap.
findings.violated_requirement: Explicit declaration of custody consequences for semantic-only sources
